findings.topic: Scope and ground truth
findings.fact: All claims below are from HEAD 3208d29 on branch audit/mainnet-hardening. Two files were read in full: consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs (3145 lines) and consensus/consensus/src/ordering.rs (1850 lines). Supporting reads: consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs (Vertex, Block), sync/src/lib.rs (ChainSync), core/node/src/main.rs (tick loops, dispatch), core/node/src/p2p.rs (gossipsub), common/storage/src/lib.rs, and the vendored libp2p-gossipsub-0.47.0 source for one transport claim.
findings.evidence: `git rev-parse --short HEAD` = 3208d29; `wc -l` = 3145 /Users/macbookpro/Documents/AINCORE-Blockchain/consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs, 1850 /Users/macbookpro/Documents/AINCORE-Blockchain/consensus/consensus/src/ordering.rs

findings.topic: STATE MODEL — the per-node data structures that define a hash's state
findings.fact: A vertex hash H, as seen by one node, is a function of exactly four stores: (1) in-memory `dag: HashMap<String, Vertex>` and `round_index: HashMap<u64, Vec<String>>`; (2) RocksDB row `vertex:{hash}`; (3) the ordering engine's `committed_set` (HashSet mirror of the bounded `committed_sequence`) plus per-round `consensus:cseq:{round}` rows; (4) nothing else — there is NO data structure recording a hash that is cited but absent (no orphan/missing/park set exists at HEAD; the only mentions of 'orphan'/'park' in dag.rs are comments about the reverted attempts and the mempool loan ledger).
findings.evidence: /Users/macbookpro/Documents/AINCORE-Blockchain/consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:51-52 `pub dag: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, Vertex>>>, // Hash -> Vertex` / `pub round_index: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<u64, Vec<String>>>>`; dag.rs:1177 `.put(&format!("vertex:{}", vertex.hash), &v_json)`; /Users/macbookpro/Documents/AINCORE-Blockchain/consensus/consensus/src/ordering.rs:44-48 `pub committed_sequence: Vec<String>` / `committed_set: std::collections::HashSet<String>`; ordering.rs:92 `const COMMITTED_SEQ_KEY_PREFIX: &str = "consensus:cseq:"`; grep 'missing|orphan|park' in dag.rs returns only comment lines 26, 99, 626, 1096-1110, 1256, 1761, 2069.
findings.implication_for_design: Any fetch design must ADD the fifth store (a bounded 'wanted parents' index keyed by hash) — it cannot be derived from existing state, and its absence is why a hole is only ever discovered by re-walking history.

findings.topic: STATE MODEL — the six states
findings.fact: S0 UNKNOWN: not in dag, no vertex: row, not in committed_set. S1 IN_DAG: dag[H] present AND round_index[H.round] contains H AND vertex:H row present (all three written together at admission). S2 COMMITTED/SETTLED: H ∈ committed_set (and a cseq row for its anchor round); may or may not also be in dag — S2 is reachable WITHOUT a body via sync adoption. S3 PRUNED: removed from dag, round_index, and vertex: row by prune_dag; may linger in committed_set until window eviction. S4 DROPPED_AS_EQUIVOCATION: rejected in the double-sign branch; never inserted, never persisted; the only durable trace is a compact proof under sys:equiv_seen whose payload AND parents are stripped. S5 REJECTED_AT_INGRESS (transient or permanent sub-classes, enumerated separately). S6 CITED_BUT_ABSENT: a DERIVED condition — some vertex in dag lists H in `parents` while H is in S0/S3/S4/S5 and H ∉ committed_set. It is recognized only transiently inside walk_history/find_causal_history/direct_quorum_met and is stored nowhere.
findings.evidence: S1 write set: dag.rs:1174-1187 (`vertex:` put, `dag.insert`, `round_idx.entry(...).push`). S2 without body: ordering.rs:869-888 `adopt_synced_anchor(... sequence: &[String] ...)` → ordering.rs:795 `self.record_committed(&sequence)`. S3: dag.rs:2770-2783. S4: dag.rs:1143-1167 (return before the persist at 1174) + dag.rs:2307 `(first.to_compact_proof(), second.to_compact_proof())` and /Users/macbookpro/Documents/AINCORE-Blockchain/consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs:454-461 `c.payload = Vec::new(); c.parents = Vec::new();`. S6 recognition: ordering.rs:697-702, 975, 665-669.
findings.implication_for_design: The design's state machine must treat S2-without-body as a first-class settled state (it is how sync heals cursors today) and must decide explicitly whether S4 is terminal or fetchable, because today S4 is a hole that no message type can fill.

findings.topic: TRANSITION S0→S1 (admission) — the full ingress gate, in order
findings.fact: add_vertex admits a remote vertex only after: (1) round ≤ u64::MAX/2; (2) round ≤ current_round + 10_000; (3) timestamp ≤ now + 30 s; (4) author pubkey resolvable from the account object in storage (or self); (5) Ed25519 signature over the hash valid; (6) aggregated_signature is None; (7) live form (no payload_root/parents_root); (8) ≤ 256 parents, no duplicates; (9) hash == recomputed body hash; (10) author in the current validator set; (11) hash not already in dag; (12) no other vertex from the same author at the same round. There is NO check that any parent exists, NO check that parents belong to round-1, and NO check that a parent string is a well-formed hash.
findings.evidence: /Users/macbookpro/Documents/AINCORE-Blockchain/consensus/consensus/src/dag.rs:952 `if vertex.round > Self::ABSOLUTE_ROUND_CEILING`; :964 `if vertex.round > self.current_round.saturating_add(Self::MAX_ROUND_JUMP)`; :980-991 `MAX_FUTURE_DRIFT_SECS: u64 = 30`; :999-1002 `resolve_author_pubkey`; :1004 `verify_ed25519_signature`; :1026 `aggregated_signature.is_some()`; :1036 `!vertex.is_live_form()`; :1046-1061 MAX_PARENTS + uniq; :1062-1070 recomputed hash; :1082 `!validators.contains(&vertex.author)`; :1126 `dag.contains_key(&vertex.hash)`; :1143-1168 equivocation. The only uses of `parents` in add_vertex are :1046, :1057 (grep 'parents' dag.rs).
findings.implication_for_design: The malicious-parent attack needs no bug: a validator key plus a 64-hex string that hashes nothing is sufficient. A design that keeps verbatim citation must add a parent-resolution gate at THIS point in the sequence (after 12), with a bounded wait plus fetch — not a drop.

findings.topic: TRANSITION S0→S1 via the three boot recovery loops
findings.fact: On construction, DagConsensus rebuilds dag/round_index from disk by three loops: (A) checkpoint loop — only if a signed checkpoint at `dag:checkpoint:latest` verifies against THIS node's key; (B) tail loop — every `vertex:` row with round > checkpoint_round not already loaded; (C) legacy loop — every `vertex:` row when no checkpoint exists. All three apply: hash-integrity, live-form, and refuse a second vertex from the same author at the same round. current_round is then max(max_loaded_round+1, latest_proposed_round+1). None of the loops can produce a vertex that was not persisted by add_vertex, and none consults committed_set.
findings.evidence: dag.rs:122 `let checkpoint_round = storage.get_latest_checkpoint_round();`; loop A dag.rs:211-253; loop B dag.rs:273-320 `for v_json in storage.scan_vertices() { ... if vertex.round <= checkpoint_round || dag_map.contains_key(&vertex.hash) { continue; }`; loop C dag.rs:331-373; equivocation refusal in all three at :231-242, :297-308, :352-363; round restore :422-434 `final_start_round = explicit_max_round + 1`. Checkpoint content is `dag.values()` sorted by hash: dag.rs:1828-1829; written only when `self.current_round.is_multiple_of(100)` inside the commit path: dag.rs:1819.
findings.implication_for_design: A restart cannot manufacture a missing vertex; it can only re-load what this node admitted. A restart CAN, however, drop a vertex the checkpoint held if a tampered/unsigned checkpoint forces the scan path and the vertex row was already pruned (not a hole source in normal operation, but the design's 'restart' case must assume the post-restart DAG ⊆ the pre-restart DAG).

findings.topic: TRANSITION S1→S2 (local commit) and S0→S2 (settled via sync)
findings.fact: Locally, a hash enters committed_set only through apply_anchor_bookkeeping→record_committed, called from commit_one_anchor with the anchor's causal history (filtered to exclude already-committed hashes). Via sync, reload_chain_tip iterates every synced block above last_adopted_height and calls adopt_synced_anchor(block.header.round, &block.anchor_hash, &block.committed_vertices, ...), which records the block's committed_vertices VERBATIM into committed_set — bodies are never transferred (Block.committed_vertices is Vec<String> of hashes; SyncResponse carries blocks only). adopt is a no-op when anchor_round <= finalized_round or already in committed_rounds.
findings.evidence: ordering.rs:739-748 `let mut sequence = self.find_causal_history(...); sequence.retain(|h| !self.committed_set.contains(h)); Some(self.apply_anchor_bookkeeping(...))`; ordering.rs:474-479 record_committed; dag.rs:2852-2884 `for h in start_h..=new_height { ... engine.adopt_synced_anchor(block.header.round, &block.anchor_hash, &block.committed_vertices, &validators)`; ordering.rs:876 `if anchor_round <= self.finalized_round || self.committed_rounds.contains(&anchor_round) { return None; }`; /Users/macbookpro/Documents/AINCORE-Blockchain/consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs:42 `pub committed_vertices: Vec<String>`; /Users/macbookpro/Documents/AINCORE-Blockchain/sync/src/lib.rs:16-27 `pub struct SyncResponse { pub blocks: Vec<Block>, ... }`.
findings.implication_for_design: Sync adoption is the ONLY existing mechanism that converts a hole into 'settled', and it works precisely because walk_history treats committed_set membership as settled without needing the body. But it requires that SOME validator built a block past the hole — which is impossible when every validator shares the hole.

findings.topic: TRANSITION S2→(not settled): when a hash FALLS OUT of committed_set
findings.fact: Two eviction paths. (1) Live: record_committed drains the oldest entries once committed_sequence exceeds COMMITTED_SEQ_WINDOW = 8192 hashes and removes them from committed_set. (2) Restart: committed_set is rebuilt ONLY from `consensus:cseq:{round}` rows for rounds still inside committed_rounds, which is trimmed to the most recent COMMITTED_ROUNDS_WINDOW = 256 anchor rounds; cseq rows for evicted rounds are deleted at commit time. So after a restart the set covers at most 256 anchor rounds (≈2·n vertices each), which is generally SMALLER than the 8192-hash live window.
findings.evidence: ordering.rs:90 `const COMMITTED_SEQ_WINDOW: usize = 8192;`; ordering.rs:480-485 `for h in self.committed_sequence.drain(0..excess) { self.committed_set.remove(&h); }`; ordering.rs:82 `const COMMITTED_ROUNDS_WINDOW: u64 = 256;`; ordering.rs:781-793 cutoff/retain; ordering.rs:817-819 `storage.delete(&format!("{}{}", COMMITTED_SEQ_KEY_PREFIX, r))`; restart rebuild ordering.rs:158-175 `for r in recent { if let Ok(Some(json)) = storage.get(&format!("{}{}", COMMITTED_SEQ_KEY_PREFIX, r))`.
findings.implication_for_design: A hash that is BOTH pruned from dag (S3) AND evicted from committed_set becomes indistinguishable from S0 — a hole — if anything still cites it. Honest vertices never cite that old, but ingress does not bound parent age, so a malicious vertex citing an ancient real hash is a second, cheaper hole vector. The design must either bound parent round at ingress (round-1 only) or make the settled test age-independent.

findings.topic: TRANSITION S1→S3 (prune) — what is deleted and the exact condition
findings.fact: prune_dag(min_round) deletes from memory every dag entry with vertex.round < min_round, deletes the RocksDB row vertex:{hash} for each (fsync'd delete), and drops round_index keys < min_round. It is called from exactly one production site: inside the commit loop after a block is locally BUILT, only when latest_block_height % 10 == 0 AND current_round > 50, with min_round = min(engine.finalized_round, latest_block_round) - 10 (and only if that horizon > 10). It is never called from the sync path, never on a timer, and never on observer nodes.
findings.evidence: dag.rs:2770-2783 `if vertex.round < min_round { to_remove.push(...) } ... self.storage.delete(&format!("vertex:{}", hash)); dag.remove(hash); ... round_idx.retain(|r, _| *r >= min_round);`; dag.rs:1786 `if self.latest_block_height.is_multiple_of(10) && self.current_round > 50`; dag.rs:1806-1808 `let horizon = finalized_round.min(self.latest_block_round); if horizon > 10 { self.prune_dag(horizon - 10); }`; call sites: grep `prune_dag(` → only dag.rs:1808 (+ tests); storage delete fsync: /Users/macbookpro/Documents/AINCORE-Blockchain/common/storage/src/lib.rs:135-140.
findings.implication_for_design: Because pruning is gated on a LOCAL block build, a wedged node never prunes — so the vertex that carries the bad parent (and the first vertex of an equivocating pair) stays in round_index forever on a wedged node. A fetch design can rely on peers that ARE progressing to still hold vertices for ≥10 rounds past finality; that is the serving window a VERTEX_REQ has.

findings.topic: walk_history — exact settled predicate and the hole return
findings.fact: walk_history(from, floor, _, dag, committed_set) does a DFS from `from`. For a popped hash h: if dag.get(h) is None, then h is SETTLED iff h == "genesis" OR committed_set.contains(h) (continue); otherwise it returns None (HOLE) immediately. For a present vertex v it records it, stops descending when v.round <= floor, and pushes each parent p unless p == "genesis" or committed_set.contains(p). The from_round argument is unused. Note the literal string "genesis" is settled at ANY round, so a vertex citing "genesis" at round 500 is not a hole.
findings.evidence: ordering.rs:683-714, specifically :697-702 `let Some(v) = dag.get(&h) else { if h == "genesis" || committed_set.contains(&h) { continue; // settled — not a hole } return None; // hole };` and :704 `if v.round <= floor { continue; }` and :707-711 `for p in &v.parents { if p != "genesis" && !committed_set.contains(p) { stack.push(p.clone()); } }`; :690 `let _ = from_round;`.
findings.implication_for_design: The settled predicate is exactly {in dag} ∪ {genesis} ∪ committed_set. A design that introduces a 'known-unresolvable, safe to skip' verdict must extend THIS predicate deterministically (identically on every node), or it will fork: any node-local decision here changes the committed sequence.

findings.topic: commit_one_anchor — what happens on a hole
findings.fact: commit_one_anchor first requires the anchor vertex itself to be in dag (else None), then calls walk_history(anchor, floor=0, ...) with the `?` operator: a None from walk_history returns None from commit_one_anchor before ANY state is touched (no cursor move, no committed_rounds insert, no digest fold, no persistence). Only on Some does it compute find_causal_history, filter committed, and run apply_anchor_bookkeeping. Floor 0 means the walk descends the ENTIRE uncommitted causal cone — every uncommitted ancestor at any depth is checked for presence.
findings.evidence: ordering.rs:730 `let anchor_round_in_dag = dag.get(anchor_vertex_hash).map(|v| v.round)?;`; ordering.rs:731-737 `Self::walk_history(anchor_vertex_hash, 0, anchor_round_in_dag, dag, &self.committed_set)?;`; ordering.rs:739-748.
findings.implication_for_design: A hole anywhere in the uncommitted cone blocks the anchor; the cone is bounded only by committed_set. Therefore the practical depth of a hole's damage is 'everything since the last committed anchor', and the design's fetch must be able to resolve holes at arbitrary depth below the anchor, not just direct parents.

findings.topic: try_commit — scan, skip-walk, and every path that yields nothing
findings.fact: try_commit decides ONE anchor per call, starting at start = align_anchor(next_anchor_round) (even rounds only). Step 1 scans even r from start while r < max_round (max key of round_index) and r - start < 10_000 for the smallest r whose leader vertex is in dag AND has direct stake-quorum votes at r+1; if none, returns empty. Step 2 walks BACK over even j in [start, r_direct): for each j it calls walk_history(chain, floor=j, ...) — a None (hole between j and the chain anchor) returns EMPTY for the whole call; otherwise j commits if its leader vertex is in the visited set, else it is skipped silently. Step 3 commits only the LOWEST decidable anchor via commit_one_anchor; a None there also yields empty. Nothing is persisted on the empty paths, so the next call re-derives from the same cursor.
findings.evidence: ordering.rs:554 `let start = Self::align_anchor(self.next_anchor_round.max(1));`; :545 `let max_round = round_index.keys().copied().max().unwrap_or(0);`; :548 `const MAX_SCAN: u64 = 10_000;`; :558-567 `while r < max_round && r - start < MAX_SCAN { if let Some(h) = Self::leader_vertex_hash(...) { if Self::direct_quorum_met(...) { direct = Some((r, h)); break; } } r += 2; }`; :568-570 `let Some((r_direct, direct_hash)) = direct else { return out; };`; :576-598 skip-walk with :581-586 `else { // HOLE below the chain anchor: not decidable yet. return out; }`; :607-617 `to_commit.reverse(); ... if let Some(info) = self.commit_one_anchor(...) { out.push(info); }`.
findings.implication_for_design: There is no partial progress and no memo: a hole costs a full DFS on every retry, and retries happen on every admitted vertex (see next finding). A fetch design should record WHICH hash walk_history failed on (return Err(hash) instead of None) so the wanted-set is populated at zero extra cost.

findings.topic: Retry cadence — when try_commit is re-run
findings.fact: try_commit is invoked only from add_vertex, after a vertex is admitted (local or remote), for validator nodes; it loops until it returns empty. It is NOT run on the consensus ticker, NOT run after reload_chain_tip adopts anchors, and NOT run for observers. So a hole is 're-tested' exactly once per admitted vertex.
findings.evidence: dag.rs:1248-1258 observer early-return; dag.rs:1273-1295 `loop { let commit = { ... let mut batch = engine.try_commit(vertex.round, &dag, &round_idx, &validators); if batch.is_empty() { break; } batch.remove(0) };`; /Users/macbookpro/Documents/AINCORE-Blockchain/core/node/src/main.rs:680-684 ticker calls only `c.try_create_vertex()`; main.rs:1036-1040 sync loop calls only `c.reload_chain_tip()`; reload_chain_tip (dag.rs:2815-3014) never calls try_commit.
findings.implication_for_design: When a fetched vertex is admitted through add_vertex, the existing retry fires automatically — so a VERTEX_RESP handler that feeds add_vertex needs no extra commit trigger. Conversely, adopting anchors via sync does not retry local commit until the next gossip vertex arrives.

findings.topic: direct_quorum_met and leader_vertex_hash under a missing vertex
findings.fact: direct_quorum_met counts, over round_index[round+1], the distinct authors of vertices PRESENT in dag whose parents contain anchor_hash, weighted by stake, and requires signed*3 > total*2. A missing r+1 vertex simply does not vote; a missing anchor (leader) vertex makes leader_vertex_hash None, so that round cannot be a direct anchor at all. Neither function ever inspects whether the r+1 voters' OWN parents resolve.
findings.evidence: ordering.rs:658-675 `let Some(votes) = round_index.get(&(round + 1)) else { return false; }; ... if let Some(v) = dag.get(vh) { if v.parents.iter().any(|p| p == anchor_hash) { voted.insert(v.author.as_str()); } }`; /Users/macbookpro/Documents/AINCORE-Blockchain/consensus/consensus/src/qc.rs:194-196 `signed_stake.saturating_mul(3) > total_stake.saturating_mul(2)`; ordering.rs:634-646 leader_vertex_hash.
findings.implication_for_design: Missing votes degrade liveness gracefully (anchor may still commit or be skipped later by ancestry), but a missing LEADER that IS cited by r+1 voters is the test_b4b_missing_voted_leader case: deferral forever until fetched. The fetch design's highest-value target is the leader vertex of the lowest undecided even round.

findings.topic: quorum_round and parent_quorum_met — effect of a missing vertex
findings.fact: quorum_round returns the highest round r for which the distinct authors of round_index[r] vertices that are PRESENT in dag hold > 2/3 of stake. parent_quorum_met in try_create_vertex applies the same stake test to the chosen parents (round_index[current_round-1]) via dag lookup. A hash in round_index that is not in dag is skipped (contributes nothing); since round_index and dag are always written together, this only differs after a partial prune. A missing vertex therefore lowers the counted stake but never blocks; a vertex citing a non-existent parent COUNTS fully toward both quorums.
findings.evidence: dag.rs:493-525 quorum_round `for h in hashes { if let Some(v) = dag.get(h) { authors.insert(v.author.as_str()); } } ... if crate::qc::stake_quorum_met(round_stake, total_stake) { best = *round; }`; dag.rs:566-585 parent_quorum_met `for ph in &parents { if let Some(v) = dag.get(ph) { authors.insert(v.author.as_str()); } }`.
findings.implication_for_design: Round advance and proposal are decoupled from hole resolution: a node keeps proposing (and keeps propagating the hole) even while its commit cursor is wedged. That is the mechanism by which one bad vertex reaches every node's cone.

findings.topic: try_create_vertex — parents are round_index[prev] VERBATIM
findings.fact: The parent list is `round_index[current_round - 1]` cloned as-is (truncated to 256 by hash sort only if larger), plus the literal "genesis" at prev_round 0. No filter by resolved history, no filter by author, no exclusion of vertices whose own parents are holes.
findings.evidence: dag.rs:529-536 `let prev_round = self.current_round - 1; let mut parents = { ... round_idx.get(&prev_round).cloned().unwrap_or_default() };`; :542-545 truncate; :548-550 genesis; :719-728 `Vertex { ... parents, ... }`.
findings.implication_for_design: This single line (535) is the propagation vector for both the malicious hole and the equivocation hole. Narwhal's rule is to reference only vertices whose full causal history the proposer holds; adopting that rule here converts an attacker's vertex from 'wedges everyone' to 'wedges nobody, is simply never cited'. Parent sets may then differ per node, which is safe for Bullshark (only the ≥2/3 overlap matters) but must be checked against direct_quorum_met and the skip-proof.

findings.topic: try_create_vertex else-branch — exact re-gossip window and trigger
findings.fact: Re-gossip runs ONLY when this node is an active validator, has peers (or is singleton), AND parent_quorum_met is false at its current round. It then broadcasts every vertex in its OWN dag with round >= current_round.saturating_sub(3) (a 4-round window), once per consensus tick (default 3000 ms, env AINCORE_CONSENSUS_TICK_MS, min 100). It is a PUSH of what the node already holds; a node above parent quorum never enters this branch regardless of what its peers are missing.
findings.evidence: dag.rs:608-618 observer / isolated returns; :621 `if parent_quorum_met {` ... :881 `} else {`; :908-915 `let min_round = self.current_round.saturating_sub(3); dag.values().filter(|v| v.round >= min_round).cloned().collect()`; :922-924 `for v in &resend { self.broadcast_vertex(v); }`; tick: /Users/macbookpro/Documents/AINCORE-Blockchain/core/node/src/main.rs:633-637, 683-686.
findings.implication_for_design: This loop can never deliver a vertex to a node that lacks it unless the HOLDER happens to be below parent quorum — the inversion documented at dag.rs:1100-1106. Any design must add a pull. The 4-round window is also too shallow for holes below the cursor (walk depth is 'since last commit', which on a stalled follower can be hundreds of rounds).

findings.topic: Transport fact — a re-gossiped identical vertex is silently NOT published on gossipsub for 60 s
findings.fact: Gossipsub is configured with message_id = SHA-256 of the payload and duplicate_cache_time = 60 s. The node's publish call ignores the result. In libp2p-gossipsub 0.47.0, publish() returns Err(PublishError::Duplicate) when the message id is already in the duplicate cache. Hence a re-gossip of a byte-identical DAG_VERTEX within 60 s of its first publish is dropped locally on the gossipsub path, and only the TCP fallback (which requires a `peer_ip` row; default 127.0.0.1) can carry it.
findings.evidence: /Users/macbookpro/Documents/AINCORE-Blockchain/core/node/src/p2p.rs:119-123 `.duplicate_cache_time(Duration::from_secs(60)) .message_id_fn(|msg| { ... MessageId::from(Sha256::digest(&msg.data).to_vec()) })`; p2p.rs:275 `let _ = swarm.behaviour_mut().gossipsub.publish(IdentTopic::new("aincore-gossip"), msg.as_bytes());`; /Users/macbookpro/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/libp2p-gossipsub-0.47.0/src/behaviour.rs:610-617 `if self.duplicate_cache.contains(&msg_id) { ... return Err(PublishError::Duplicate); }`; TCP fallback dag.rs:1904-1920 `.get_peer_ip(peer_id).unwrap_or_else(|| "127.0.0.1".to_string())`.
findings.implication_for_design: A VERTEX_RESP must NOT be a byte-identical DAG_VERTEX re-publish — it must be a distinct message (different bytes → different id) or a direct TCP/stream reply, otherwise the dedup cache defeats redelivery. Also: the existing re-gossip loop is largely a TCP-only mechanism during the first minute, which explains why multi-machine bootstrap depended on peer_ip persistence.

findings.topic: Transport fact — inbound rate limiting DROPS vertices without any record
findings.fact: Inbound gossipsub messages are dropped (never banned) when a relaying connection exceeds 2000 msg/s aggregate or an authenticated publisher exceeds 100 msg/s. A dropped DAG_VERTEX is invisible to consensus; nothing schedules a re-request. This is a benign, no-attacker source of S0 for vertices the rest of the network holds.
findings.evidence: p2p.rs:255 `const MAX_MSG_PER_SEC: u32 = 100;`; :264 `const MAX_CONN_MSG_PER_SEC: u32 = 2_000;`; :345-352 `if *c_count > MAX_CONN_MSG_PER_SEC { ... continue; // drop this message only; never ban a relay }`; :391-398 `if *count > MAX_MSG_PER_SEC { ... continue; // drop only }`.
findings.implication_for_design: Ordinary loss is by design, so the fetch path is not an edge case — it is the steady-state repair mechanism and must be cheap enough to run continuously (bounded by wanted-set size, not by vertex rate).

findings.topic: reload_chain_tip — the round cap and the catch-up floor (quoted)
findings.fact: After a synced tip at block round R: tip_next = R+1; quorum_target = quorum_round(...)+1; catchup_floor = tip_next − MAX_ROUND_JUMP/2 = tip_next − 5000; next_round = min(tip_next, max(quorum_target, catchup_floor)); current_round is raised (never lowered) to next_round and persisted as latest_proposed_round. It also raises latest_block_round to max(existing, R), SETS latest_block_timestamp, invalidates the validator cache, and — only when new_height > latest_block_height — adopts every block in (last_adopted_height, new_height] into the ordering engine, breaking at the first block missing from storage.
findings.evidence: dag.rs:2998-3000 `let tip_next = round.saturating_add(1); let catchup_floor = tip_next.saturating_sub(Self::MAX_ROUND_JUMP / 2); let next_round = tip_next.min(quorum_target.max(catchup_floor));`; :946 `const MAX_ROUND_JUMP: u64 = 10_000;`; :3001-3011 raise+persist; :2945 `self.latest_block_round = self.latest_block_round.max(r);`; :2956 `self.latest_block_timestamp = ts;`; :2825 `if new_height > self.latest_block_height {`; :2852-2861 `for h in start_h..=new_height { let Some(block) = ... else { break; };`.
findings.implication_for_design: A stranded node's proposal clock can sit up to 5000 rounds below the network tip while its DAG refills by gossip — but gossip refill cannot happen for vertices already pruned by progressing peers (finality−10). So a node more than ~10 rounds behind cannot rebuild parent quorum from gossip at all; it depends entirely on sync adoption to move its cursor, and on NEW vertices to resume proposing. The design's fetch must serve at least the peers' unpruned window and the design should state what happens beyond it (state-sync, not vertex-sync).

findings.topic: Equivocation branch — fate of the second vertex, and what a peer that already cited it experiences
findings.fact: When a vertex B arrives with the same author and round as an existing A but a different hash, add_vertex calls apply_equivocation_slash(A,B) (writes sys:equiv_seen with COMPACT proofs, queues evidence, writes validator:jailed) and broadcast_equivocation_proof, then RETURNS before persisting or inserting B. B is in S4 on this node. Every later re-delivery of B takes the same branch (A is still in round_index; apply short-circuits on sys:equiv_seen; the broadcast at :1166 is NOT latched and repeats). Meanwhile a peer that received B first holds B and drops A; its next vertex cites B verbatim. On this node, that peer's vertex is admitted (no parent check) and any walk through it hits B → None. Symmetrically the peer sees holes at A. Neither B nor A can ever be admitted on the other side while the counterpart is in round_index, and round_index is only cleared by prune, which requires a local block build, which the hole prevents.
findings.evidence: dag.rs:1143-1168 `if v_exist.author == vertex.author && existing_hash != &vertex.hash { ... self.apply_equivocation_slash(&proof_a, &proof_b); self.broadcast_equivocation_proof(&proof_a, &proof_b); return; }`; persist happens after at :1174; dedup latch dag.rs:2287-2290 `let seen_key = format!("sys:equiv_seen:{}:{}", offender, round); if matches!(self.storage.get(&seen_key), Ok(Some(_))) { return; }`; compact proof stripping :2307 and blockchain lib.rs:454-461; gossip latch exists only in handle_remote_equivocation :2445-2454; verbatim citation dag.rs:535; prune gate dag.rs:1786-1808.
findings.implication_for_design: Equivocation is a THIRD hole source, and it is the one a fetch cannot heal: a VERTEX_REQ for B would be answered by the peer that holds B, but this node's ingress would reject it again. Bullshark tolerates equivocation because vertices carry certificates (2f+1 signatures) and only certified vertices are cited; AINCORE has no certificates, so the design must choose: (a) admit both equivocating vertices into dag (they are both signed, both hash-bound) and rely on the deterministic slash + the ordering rule, or (b) add a pre-citation rule that never cites a vertex whose author is known to have equivocated at that round. Option (a) is the smaller change and is how the evidence path already treats them (both proofs verify).

findings.topic: Ingress does NOT bound parent round or parent age
findings.fact: Nothing in add_vertex relates `vertex.parents` to `vertex.round - 1` or to any round. Combined with committed_set eviction and prune, a validator can cite (i) a fabricated hash (permanent hole), (ii) the hash of a real vertex that has been pruned AND evicted from committed_set on every node (permanent hole, indistinguishable from (i)), or (iii) "genesis" at any round (always settled). Honest vertices only ever cite the previous round.
findings.evidence: grep 'parents' in dag.rs shows the only ingress uses are :1046 (`vertex.parents.len() > MAX_PARENTS`) and :1057 (uniqueness); producer side :535 uses round_index[prev_round]; walk_history genesis sentinel ordering.rs:698, 708.
findings.implication_for_design: Add an ingress invariant: every parent must be resolvable to a vertex at exactly round−1 (or the genesis sentinel only at round 1). This turns 'cited-but-absent' into a question with a bounded answer window (one round) and makes the fetch target set well-defined: for a vertex at round r, wanted = parents ∖ (dag ∪ committed_set), all at round r−1.

findings.topic: The malicious hole, traced end-to-end through the code
findings.fact: Attacker (validator key) emits V at round r with parents = [P] where P is a 64-hex string that no vertex has. V passes all 12 ingress checks and is inserted (S1) on every node that receives it. At round r+1 every honest node cites round_index[r] verbatim, including V. Anchor r (if even) still commits — its history is below V. The next anchor at r+2 has all r+1 vertices as parents; commit_one_anchor walks from it (floor 0) → r+1 vertices → V → P: P ∉ dag, P ≠ "genesis", P ∉ committed_set → None. try_commit returns empty; cursor stays at r+2 forever. If the attacker delivers V to only a subset S of nodes, nodes outside S do not have V but DO admit S's r+1 vertices (which cite V) → V itself is their hole; every node is wedged either at P or at V. No block is built by anyone, so no sync adoption can move any cursor, and no prune runs, so V/P never age out.
findings.evidence: Admission: dag.rs:1046-1070 (no parent existence check), :1174-1187 insert. Citation: dag.rs:535. Walk: ordering.rs:697-702, 731-737. No block → no adopt: dag.rs:2875-2884 requires a stored block; no prune: dag.rs:1786-1808 inside the local block-build path only.
findings.implication_for_design: Two independent defenses are needed and both are cheap: (1) do not cite a vertex until its parents are resolved locally (bounded wait + fetch), so V is never propagated by honest proposers; (2) an ingress bound that turns 'unresolvable after fetch from ≥ f+1 peers within T' into a deterministic local non-citation (not a global skip — the vertex stays admitted so the skip-proof remains sound if a peer does have P). Slashing is not required for liveness under (1).

findings.topic: The honest hole, traced end-to-end through the code
findings.fact: Honest vertex X at round r is lost in transit to node N (packet loss, rate-limit drop, restart, gossipsub dedup on a re-send). Peers cite X at r+1; N admits those. N's next anchor walk hits X → None → N's cursor stalls. N keeps proposing (parent quorum counts only present vertices, and > 2/3 is usually still met), so N is not ejected, but it commits nothing locally. Repair today: (a) X's holder re-gossips ONLY if that holder itself drops below parent quorum (rare on a healthy network) and only within 4 rounds, and only over TCP within 60 s; (b) a peer that is NOT stalled builds a block for the anchor, N imports it via ChainSync, reload_chain_tip adopts the sequence (which contains X's hash) into committed_set, and N's walk now treats X as settled — this is the burn-in fix and it is why the chain survives honest holes today.
findings.evidence: Loss sources: p2p.rs:345-352, 391-398 (drop), p2p.rs:119-123 + libp2p-gossipsub-0.47.0/src/behaviour.rs:610-617 (dedup). Re-gossip gating: dag.rs:621, 881-926. Sync heal: dag.rs:2843-2884, ordering.rs:869-888, ordering.rs:698 `committed_set.contains(&h)`. Proposal continues: dag.rs:566-585.
findings.implication_for_design: The honest case is already healed by sync AS LONG AS ≥1 validator is unaffected; it fails only when the SAME vertex is missing on every validator (bootstrap, small n, correlated loss) — exactly the case dag.rs:1100-1108 describes for the 'drop' attempt. A pull mechanism closes the residual; it does not need to replace sync adoption.

findings.topic: For a vertex this node DROPPED — every path by which it could become resolvable today, with verdicts
findings.fact: Definition: 'dropped' = the hash is S0/S4/S5 here while some admitted vertex cites it. Paths: (1) Peer re-gossip loop → possible ONLY if a holder is below parent quorum AND the vertex is within that holder's last 4 rounds AND (within 60 s) the TCP fallback reaches N; the holder must have `peer_ip` for N. (2) Original author's one-shot broadcast at creation → already happened; never repeated. (3) ChainSync block import → cannot deliver the body, but CAN make the hash SETTLED via adopt_synced_anchor — possible only if some validator built a block whose committed_vertices contains it; impossible if every validator shares the hole. (4) Boot recovery loops → impossible: only vertices this node persisted are replayed, and persistence happens after all ingress checks. (5) EQUIV_PROOF gossip → impossible: proofs are compact (payload and parents stripped) and ingress rejects proof-form vertices. (6) A VERTEX_REQ/VERTEX_RESP → does not exist anywhere in the tree. (7) Re-delivery of an S4 (equivocation-dropped) vertex → impossible while its counterpart is in round_index; round_index is cleared only by prune, which requires a local block. (8) Re-delivery of an S5-transient vertex (author pubkey not yet in storage, author not yet in the local validator set, timestamp > now+30 s at receipt) → possible only via (1), after local state catches up. (9) Re-delivery of an S5-permanent vertex (bad signature, hash mismatch, proof-form, > 256 or duplicate parents, oversize) → impossible and correct: the vertex is not a valid vertex on any node.
findings.evidence: (1) dag.rs:621, 881-926, 1904-1920; p2p.rs:119-123; libp2p-gossipsub-0.47.0/src/behaviour.rs:610-617. (2) dag.rs:749-750. (3) dag.rs:2852-2884; ordering.rs:869-888; blockchain lib.rs:42; sync/src/lib.rs:16-27, 1211-1248. (4) dag.rs:211-253, 273-320, 331-373 with persist at 1174-1181. (5) dag.rs:2307, 2370-2371; blockchain lib.rs:454-461; dag.rs:1036-1042. (6) grep VERTEX_REQ → only comments dag.rs:1105, 1111; inbound prefixes are exactly DAG_VERTEX/DOWNTIME_ATTEST/EQUIV_PROOF/QC_VOTE (dag.rs:2558-2586) + TX/DA_COMMIT/DA_SHARD/GET_HEIGHT/GET_FINALITY/SYNC_REQ (main.rs:702-801). (7) dag.rs:1143-1168, 2287-2290, 1786-1808. (8) dag.rs:999-1002, 1082-1088, 980-991. (9) dag.rs:1004-1010, 1026-1070, 2562-2569.
findings.implication_for_design: Only (1), (3), (8) are live, and (1) is gated on the WRONG node's state. The design must (a) add (6) as a distinct message pair, (b) make (7) either fetchable-and-admissible or non-citable, and (c) keep (3) as the settled-without-body path because it is the only one that scales to 'the network already decided'.

findings.topic: What a fetched vertex would go through if a VERTEX_RESP fed add_vertex unchanged
findings.fact: If a peer returned the exact live vertex, add_vertex would re-run all 12 checks. Checks that can fail for a LEGITIMATE vertex on the fetching node: (2) round jump (only if the node is > 10_000 rounds behind — mitigated by the catch-up floor), (3) timestamp drift (only if the fetcher's clock is > 30 s slow — a signed-timestamp check that is node-local, so the same vertex is admissible on one node and not another), (4)/(10) author unknown locally (state not yet synced), (12) equivocation (counterpart already held). A successful admission then re-triggers try_commit automatically.
findings.implication_for_design: Design must route fetched vertices through the SAME gate (never a side door — the reverted orphan buffer's re-entrancy hole came from bypassing it), and must treat (3) as a liveness hazard: a future-drift rejection is non-deterministic across nodes and should not apply to a vertex that a quorum already cites (or the bound should be checked at proposal time only, since timestamps are signed and bft_block_timestamp already clamps).

findings.topic: COMMIT_VERTEX_MISSING — the one place a hole is tolerated, and why it forks
findings.fact: After try_commit returns a sequence, the block builder re-reads each hash from dag under a fresh lock; a hash not found is logged as [SECURITY][COMMIT_VERTEX_MISSING] and the block is built WITHOUT its payload and timestamp sample. find_causal_history only ever emits hashes present in dag at walk time, so this can only occur if a prune ran between the walk and the build; the pruning horizon is clamped to latest_block_round to prevent it.
findings.evidence: dag.rs:1345-1385 `for hash in &commit.sequence { if let Some(v) = dag.get(hash) { ... } else { eprintln!("🚨 [SECURITY][COMMIT_VERTEX_MISSING] ...") } }`; ordering.rs:975 `if let Some(vertex) = dag.get(&hash) { history.push(hash.clone());`; dag.rs:1794-1808.
findings.implication_for_design: Any new eviction (e.g., a bounded wanted-set or a fetch-cache TTL) must never remove a vertex that is between the ordering cursor and the block builder; the safe rule already used is 'never prune above min(finalized_round, latest_block_round) − 10'.

findings.topic: Observer nodes and the hole model
findings.fact: Non-validators admit and persist vertices but never run try_commit, never build blocks, and never prune; their committed_set advances only via reload_chain_tip adoption. Their DAG therefore grows without bound and they never experience a commit wedge — but they are also not a source of repair, because the re-gossip loop returns early for observers.
findings.evidence: dag.rs:1248-1258 `if !validators.contains(&self.node_id) { ... return; }`; dag.rs:608-613 observer return before the else-branch; prune only at dag.rs:1808.
findings.implication_for_design: A VERTEX_REQ server should be allowed to run on observers (they hold the deepest unpruned history), but the fetch CLIENT logic only needs to run on validators.

findings.topic: Existing tests that pin the deferral semantics the design must preserve
findings.fact: Three ordering tests define the required behavior: a missing leader that nobody cites is SKIPPED deterministically; a missing leader that IS cited defers and later matches a full-view node exactly; a non-leader hole defers and, once filled through the same cursor, yields the identical fingerprint as a never-gapped evaluator.
findings.evidence: ordering.rs:1655-1705 test_b4b_missing_leader_is_skipped_deterministically; :1716-1759 test_b4b_missing_voted_leader_defers_instead_of_false_skip; :1764-1808 test_b4b_hole_in_history_defers_until_filled.
findings.implication_for_design: These three tests are the acceptance gate for any change to walk_history or citation: the fingerprint equality assertions must still hold, and a fourth test — 'vertex citing a never-existing parent does not wedge a node that never cites it' — is the one the new design must add.

open_questions: Citation rule change (dag.rs:535): if honest proposers cite only vertices whose full uncommitted history is locally resolved (Narwhal's rule), parent sets differ per node. direct_quorum_met (ordering.rs:650-676) and the skip-proof (ordering.rs:576-598) rely on quorum intersection, not identical parent sets — but this needs an explicit argument (and a test) that a vertex omitted by some proposers cannot flip a commit/skip decision across nodes.

Equivocation policy: should both vertices of an equivocating pair be ADMITTED into dag (both are signed and hash-bound; ordering.rs already handles multiple vertices per round) so that peers' citations of either resolve, with the slash carried as today? Or should ingress keep dropping the second and the citation rule refuse to cite an author with a sys:equiv_seen row at that round? The first is smaller; the second leaves the cross-node hole at A/B until prune.

Age bound on parents: adding 'parents must be at round−1' at ingress (or 'parents must resolve to round−1 vertices') rejects a class of vertices that today are admitted; is there any legitimate producer (e.g., a node restarted with a stale round_index) that emits parents from an older round? try_create_vertex only uses round_index[current_round−1], so apparently not — needs confirmation against reload_chain_tip's round jump (dag.rs:3000).

Fetch serving window: peers hold vertices for ≥10 rounds past min(finalized, latest_block_round) (dag.rs:1806-1808) but NOT the pruned rows; a node behind by more than that cannot be repaired by vertex fetch and must rely on sync adoption (which is already implemented). Should the design state a hard rule: 'fetch is for holes within the last N rounds; deeper holes are resolved by adopt_synced_anchor only'?

reload_chain_tip breaks the adoption loop at the first missing block (dag.rs:2859-2861) — with block-history pruning enabled (dag.rs:1662-1679), can last_adopted_height fall below the retained window on a long-offline node so that adoption (and thus settled-via-sync) never resumes? Not a hole per se, but it is the only settled-without-body path and its failure would remove the honest-hole heal.

Timestamp future-drift (dag.rs:980-991) is a node-local rejection of a signed value: two nodes with different clocks disagree on admissibility of the same vertex, which is a deterministic-hole vector without an attacker (clock skew > 30 s). Should the check move to proposal-time only, given bft_block_timestamp already clamps?

VERTEX_RESP message identity: because gossipsub dedups on SHA-256 of the payload for 60 s (p2p.rs:119-123; libp2p-gossipsub-0.47.0 behaviour.rs:610-617), a response must be byte-distinct from the original DAG_VERTEX broadcast or travel over the direct TCP channel; which transport does the design commit to, and does the TCP fallback's dependence on `peer_ip` rows (dag.rs:1909-1912) make it unreliable on fresh multi-machine clusters?
